label: Demo set, early build: the Earth Engine re-runs of 13 Oct 2026 (commit df45350), before the merge fix. Built from the files those runs saved, while Claude Code prepares the full export. Upstream of the merge it carries the open cache-grid issue (PR #42, question 1). The final re-run replaces it.

runs.note: Sanjay Van working area: a 1,300 ha rectangle (77.16 to 77.19 E, 28.51 to 28.55 N) around the park, not the park boundary.

layers.title: Kept or removed, and why

legend.label: No land-cover data in either map (not habitat)

layers.description: What the mask kept, and why it removed the rest: cropland, built-up, water or other non-habitat. Under IndiaSAT a pixel is kept or removed by a majority vote over its usable years, and a removed pixel is given the reason of its most recent non-habitat year. Other non-habitat is every remaining class: in IndiaSAT, barren land and orchard/plantation; in WorldCover, bare or sparse vegetation, snow and ice, herbaceous wetland, mangroves, and moss and lichen. This is a habitat mask, not a strict forest mask. By default it keeps IndiaSAT Trees and Shrubs/Scrub, and WorldCover tree cover, shrubland and grassland where IndiaSAT has no data; the classes a run kept are listed in its masking summary (kept_classes). The definition and the reasoning behind it are in docs/design_notes.md, section "Masking: IndiaSAT-primary, single-phase habitat".

layers.title: Which map decided each pixel
layers.description: IndiaSAT decides wherever it has at least one usable year; WorldCover decides only where IndiaSAT has no data.

summary.Shown here: Each band's mean over every stand

layers.title: NDVI seasonal amplitude, mean per stand
Radar VV minus VH (median), mean per stand
